approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves the molecular formula. After graph checks, identity normalization and duplicate rejection, it evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, and an independent archive keeps the best observation. Each selected transition installs a small, sign-balanced set of changed local motifs, ranked by whole-molecule count change and canonical description. A later neighbor is blocked when opposite inverse signs match the same stored transition.
approach.novelty: Prioritize memory for motifs rooted at the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by the selected transition. A local motif can change merely because an adjacent atom's environment changed; the current count-based ranking can give that surrounding motif a scarce slot while omitting a motif at the actual edit site. The new ranking puts changes supported at those sites first, then uses the Parent's existing ordering. Earlier siblings changed count turnover, occurrence boundaries, ring annotations, score-based credit, matching coverage or overlap retention. None used the concrete edit's atom correspondence to allocate the existing memory slots.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc completes all supplied replicas at macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population standard deviation 0.006329100643035156. Its full saved stream contains 435 selected transitions, 1711 installed slots and 195 tabu vetoes among 4545 valid novel tests. The one limiting behavior examined here is credit dilution: installation ranks global motif-count changes without locating their roots at the atoms or bond endpoints directly edited. A passive audit of every saved selected transition, using temporary atom correspondence on copies and exact identity/full-motif-count replay checks, finds only 899 of 1711 retained slots have a same-sign occurrence change among those direct roots. The proposed binary priority retains 1244 such slots, replaces 345 slots across 228 selected key sets, and changes order alone at another 62 installations, with unchanged total and per-sign capacity. Separate legacy and proposed memory tables on that fixed accepted history reproduce all 195 actual vetoes for the legacy rule; the proposed allocation yields 139 vetoes, with 69 old vetoes removed and 13 added across the 4545 recorded tests. These are unscored conditional predicate opportunities, not extra evaluated neighbors, complete alternative batches or an alternative scored walk. The earlier fractional-turnover sibling n-f37b5cf41e6f changed 104 retained key sets and 26 scored batches but lost 0.002455559942229346 in paired macro mean; its observation explicitly leaves physical edit-site credit unresolved. Count-boundary sibling n-ccfeef46a581 and cycle-annotation sibling n-9dc03aaf234b likewise changed evaluated allocation without establishing useful site-specific memory. Their failures motivate locating credit through the actual edit, without asserting that greater specificity must improve score.
hypothesis: Prioritize a selected transition's globally changed motifs whose signed occurrence changes are supported among the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by that transition, using this binary site-support priority ahead of the Parent's existing rank within its unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse-motif installation.

finding_summary.headline: Direct-site credit redirected 80 evaluations but slightly reduced the panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct edit provenance can redirect scarce memory slots and real evaluations. The unresolved issue is whether the resulting motif restrictions protect useful search behavior. Of the 373 keys added by site priority, 230 later matched a fresh molecule and 60 participated in a bidirectional veto; 105 of the 314 that expired had never matched. Full-stream source improvements increased from 468 to 475 and archive improvements from 238 to 254, while their mean positive gains fell from 0.024350 to 0.022872 and from 0.019744 to 0.018437, respectively. More locally supported credit and more small improvements therefore did not establish the registered panel benefit. A newly admitted sulfur-free aryl-amine molecule reached the DRD2 maximum of 0.949238, showing that useful conventional chemistry was accessible. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur, dense ring systems and undefined stereochemistry elsewhere, especially in the weaker sitagliptin outcome. Root provenance is not a chemical-quality test, and a later shared motif does not demonstrate reversal of the same physical site. The records identify 590 later scored descendants of the 11 changed selected states, but they cannot assign those descendant scores to one credited motif or supply the missing scores and proposals of an alternative walk.
finding_summary.results: On the same 435 selected transitions, the number of installed memory slots supported by a same-sign change at directly edited roots rose from 884 to 1,257 of 1,708 slots, or 51.76% to 73.59%. Retained keys changed at 236 installations; another 64 changed order only. Separate memory histories on the recorded Child walk produced 184 vetoes with the inherited ranking and 117 with site priority: 74 decisions became admissions and seven became additional vetoes. These changes reached 80 actually evaluated molecules across 67 batches, comprising 74 new admissions and six replacement evaluations. Twelve of those molecules improved their source, 68 worsened it, 11 became selected walk states and five improved the archive. All 435 selected-edit replays verified, with no runtime fallback. The three-seed macro mean was 0.520690, compared with 0.521759 for the Parent; the paired change was -0.001069, missing the required +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Mean endpoints improved on four tasks, but the sitagliptin decrease of 0.022009 outweighed those gains, including the DRD2 increase of 0.011290.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich molecules retain aromatic and polar frameworks, but unusual sulfur, reactive bonds and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks have trajectories. Each digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0; aromatic-token occurrence rates, in the supplied task order, are 0.9609, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7747. These are fractions of SMILES containing those tokens, not fractions of aromatic atoms or proof of feasible ring geometry. The molecules span compact fused aromatic carboxamides, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked amines, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. There is real variation across replicas and tasks, but many high-scoring examples are close relatives within these families; molecular uniqueness does not establish broad scaffold exploration. Ordinary amides, ethers, aromatic heterocycles and amines coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and highly constrained ring networks. No task has explicit charge or stereocentre tokens in optimizer proposals. Neutral SMILES can still contain basic amines; absent charge notation does not mean absent ionizability. The Parent comparison shows changes within these families and a notable sulfur-free aryl-amine maximum, without a general resolution of synthetic plausibility. Sizes and structural descriptions below come from passive parsing of the supplied trajectories; scores are recorded observations, not new calculations. The supporting audit, including input hashes and perceived structural descriptors, is .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-07-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Parsing and ring perception do not establish synthesis, stability, binding or realizable stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals have 21-29 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 46.4. Much of the chemistry retains an indole, benzofuran or benzothiophene-like framework connected through a carbonyl to a second aromatic ring, with alkoxy, methyl, amino, hydroxymethyl, thiol and halogen substituents. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide at 0.39905049777278273 has a recognizable synthetic framework. The maximum at 0.41003927643747895 is instead a benzofuran carboxamide carrying an N-chloro amide, an aminophenyl group, a thiol and an amino/chloro carbon. Other high observations and the final digest include bridged, partly unsaturated ring systems. The Parent has the same maxima in seeds 1 and 2; seed 0 changes from an aromatic sulfur-ring ketone at 0.393567030299894 to the bridged sulfur-containing ketone at 0.40196779766986834. The chemistry remains aromatic/carbonyl-centered, with substantial variation in ring feasibility and substituent reactivity.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-fluoro groups in low-scoring descendants, thiols and benzylic halides introduce reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary aromatic/carbonyl framework.
Dense closures and partially dearomatized enlarged rings create uncertain geometry and demanding synthesis; successful parsing is insufficient evidence of accessibility.
missing_features: Coverage of conventional matched carbonyl linkers and substituent patterns remains incomplete around the retained aromatic frameworks; the strong ordinary amide shows that reactive amide chlorination is not required for a high observation.
The bridged and amino/halogen-substituted products lack specified stereochemical identities. The trajectories do not show which configurations, if any, preserve the favorable arrangement.
No unseen optimal scaffold or exact missing target feature can be inferred from these comparisons alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145, whereas the ethoxy/methyl/thiol analogue reaches 0.39905049777278273. An indole/aniline product whose carbonyl has been replaced by a saturated amino-bearing connection scores 0.03343008011310944. The enlarged, partly dearomatized nitrogen-ring example scores 0.03167521481852009. Together these observations support preserving a compact aromatic-carbonyl arrangement while varying substituent placement; they do not isolate any one substituent as causal. The conventional amide already approaches the N-chloro maximum, so these observations do not establish a need for the reactive N-Cl bond. Late bridged molecules can still score poorly, including the enlarged nitrogen-ring final example at 0.04763525265209; ring closure alone does not preserve the useful arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals have 30-54 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 70.2. They retain nitrogen-rich aromatic heterocycles bearing carbonyl or thiocarbonyl groups, then accumulate substituted aryl groups, imines, alkyl chains, ethers, thioethers and halogens. The maximum at 0.6233621410649568 has 54 heavy atoms: a densely substituted phenyl group attached to a fused nitrogen heterocycle, a thiocarbonyl, a carbonyl, a terminal thiol and a long oxygen/sulfur-containing appendage ending in a chloroethyl group. Its additional sulfur center is represented with a carbon double bond and carbon/nitrogen single bonds. The final seed-2 series instead combines a dicarbonyl heterocycle, an extended unsaturated side chain and an alkoxy-substituted fused nitrogen/oxygen ring framework. These are elaborate synthetic targets rather than simple decorated drug-like cores. The Parent shows the same broad families: its seed-0 maximum 0.6161710037174721 carries an N-bromo heterocycle, whereas the Child maximum has N-methyl substitution but remains larger and sulfur-rich. The seed-2 maximum and final identity are unchanged; the Child seed-1 maximum is 0.6005174567299114 versus the Parent 0.605139548855754, with unusual sulfur chemistry still present.
liabilities: Long flexible oxygen/sulfur chains, densely substituted aryl groups and multiple imines make the highest-scoring structures complex and potentially labile.

Unusual sulfur valence remains in the leading series; reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds also occur elsewhere in the full trajectory. Removing the Parent maximum's N-Br bond does not establish overall synthetic plausibility.
missing_features: Simpler matched arrangements that preserve the retained nitrogen/carbonyl framework and attachment geometry are underexplored relative to the extensive flexible decorations; the score ties leave the necessity of those decorations unresolved.
The long-chain and multiply substituted series lacks defined stereochemical and alkene-geometric identities. No observed comparison establishes a required configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623; an early ring-reorganized analogue scores 0.526081691583997. The high series reaches 0.6233621410649568 after extensive changes to substituents and connections while retaining an aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl framework. Several alkyl-length, branch and terminal-chain variants have exactly 0.6155070237050044, and aryl-side-chain and ether-to-thioether variants share 0.6161710037174721. Thus the observed plateau does not distinguish much of the added appendage chemistry. In the final series, related molecules score 0.6092182584436399, whereas a sulfur-containing alteration of the central heterocycle scores 0.5548207448659938. Core connectivity appears more consequential than many peripheral changes; these comparisons do not identify a minimal sufficient structure.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals have 29-43 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 68.6; aromatic and ring tokens occur throughout, with halogen-token occurrence 0.9989. The high molecules combine chlorinated aromatic surfaces and non-acylated amine centers. The maximum at 0.9492384404345239 is a sulfur-free bridged aryl-amine framework with a secondary aliphatic amine linker, an aniline, an exocyclic alkene and a hydroxymethyl group. It has 32 heavy atoms and is more recognizable as medicinal chemistry than the sulfur cages, though its bridged geometry still requires scrutiny. A separate family at 0.9441493227693659 has chlorophenyl groups, a fluorinated pyrrolidine, an aminomethyl branch and unusual multiply bonded sulfur in a bridged ring system. Compared with the Parent seed-1 maximum at 0.868020189804352, the Child sulfur-free maximum loses the unusual sulfur connection while retaining aryl and amine chemistry. Seed 2 still reaches a sulfur cage, now at 0.9441493227693659 versus 0.9148143511682032; seed 0 retains sulfur-containing amine chemistry and reaches 0.808939892923393 versus 0.8856242185485628. These are chemical/score co-occurrences, not a verdict on the algorithm.
liabilities: The sulfur-cage series includes unusual S=S and hydrogen-bearing multivalent sulfur centers; another high example adds an S-Cl bond.
Bridged aryl frameworks, substituted saturated nitrogen rings and exocyclic unsaturation carry unresolved geometry and configuration, even where the heteroatom bonding is conventional.
missing_features: Conventional ring and linker alternatives that retain the successful aryl/amine spacing are incompletely represented; both a sulfur-free maximum and a tied carbon-linker analogue demonstrate that such chemistry is accessible.
Basic centers are present, but explicit protonation and stereochemical states are absent from the proposal strings. Their influence cannot be read from this unassigned, formally neutral series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The early acid/amide/sulfonamide series includes a molecule at 0.007468397818197266, whereas the later aryl-amine families reach 0.9492384404345239 and 0.9441493227693659 without those acid and acylated-amine connections. This supports the importance of how non-acylated amines are arranged relative to aromatic groups, rather than aromaticity or nitrogen presence alone: the initial compound with a basic nitrogen ring and hydroxamate scores only 0.0003786988088202195. A sulfur-centered connection and its carbon-centered analogue both score 0.9341451805829589, providing direct evidence that unusual sulfur is not required for that high-scoring arrangement. The linked sulfur cage at 0.9441493227693659 falls to 0.907358519207774 when its methylene linker is removed; amine spacing is distinguishable in this pair. These scores do not establish binding poses or protonation preferences.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals have 27-43 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 60.0. They are aromatic, carbonyl-containing polycycles with variable lactam/urea-like connections, amines, ethers and alkyl groups. The maximum at 0.20981104279018886 is a 30-heavy-atom bridged aryl/aza-aryl system containing an N-methyl lactam and an N-N-O ring connection. A different high family at 0.20784255919268485 contains a methoxy/ethoxy aza-aryl group, a phenyl ether, carbonyl-bearing rings and unusual sulfur centers. The final digest adds an aryl hydroperoxide to that family. The Parent seed-0 maximum is a related N-O-bridged lactam at 0.21196904390980506; its seed-2 maximum at 0.20185639717998205 is a sulfur-free carbonyl-rich nitrogen/oxygen polycycle, whereas the Child seed-2 maximum contains sulfur. Higher local observations do not consistently coincide with simpler chemistry.
liabilities: The high and final subsets contain peroxide or hydroperoxide bonds, unusual sulfur valence and challenging N-N-O bridges; other low-scoring proposals contain O-Cl and O-Br bonds.
Extensive bridging and medium-sized heterocyclic paths complicate synthesis and conformation. Conventional functional groups within a molecule do not validate the whole ring network.
missing_features: Matched stable heteroatom connections that preserve the constrained aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are incompletely represented beside N-N-O, peroxide and multivalent-sulfur variants.
Feasible stereochemical definitions for the bridged systems are absent; the observed structural constraints are graph constraints rather than verified three-dimensional arrangements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. Ring-opened carbonyl-chain derivatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, below the constrained aryl/carbonyl structures around 0.20775769309691736 and 0.20981104279018886. The useful distinction appears to include the arrangement and constraint of aromatic/polar groups, rather than a shortage of aromatic atoms or carbonyls. Inserting a peroxide connection into a close N-N-O relative gives 0.20647766243219587 versus 0.20775769309691736; the final aryl-hydroperoxide family still reaches 0.20769510081357428. These observations give no evidence that the score enforces peroxide avoidance. Removing a carbonyl from that late family yields 0.19623806000861144, consistent with carbonyl retention mattering locally. The narrow high-score differences do not establish a unique missing scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals have 25-33 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 62.3. Their modest atom counts conceal highly connected sulfur-rich cages, small fused rings, unsaturated bridges and nitrogen/carbonyl functionality. Aromatic-token occurrence is 0.7747, so a substantial part of the stream is fully nonaromatic. The maximum at 0.5147980244167879 has 30 heavy atoms and formula C17H15F2N3O3S5: it combines a nitrogen dicarbonyl ring, fluorinated unsaturation, multiple hydrogen-bearing multivalent sulfur centers and a thiol. The high brominated analogue at 0.4978675538217162 contains a fluorinated alcohol substituent and closely fused small rings. The seed-2 high example at 0.4413006791220245 instead contains an N-F bond, an imino group and sulfur-containing rings. These are the least conventionally plausible leading structures in the panel. The Parent also reaches sulfur cages: its seed-0 maximum is 0.48118636011729826, seed 1 is 0.5903526424693334 and seed 2 is 0.4484554129767839, compared with Child maxima 0.5147980244167879, 0.4978675538217162 and 0.4413006791220245. The family persists through these score changes.

N-F bonds occur in the seed-2 high and final series, and the final series also represents a carbon-sulfur triple bond inside a ring system. These are unusually reactive or geometrically demanding features rather than ordinary medicinal sulfur functionality.
missing_features: Conventional feasible heterocyclic alternatives that preserve the recurring nitrogen/carbonyl and fluorinated-group arrangements are largely missing from the high subset; the observed high scores reside in elaborate sulfur cages.
The cage stereochemistry and alkene geometry are unspecified. No feasible configuration or synthetic route is demonstrated for the dense ring networks.
The panel cannot establish which unseen scaffold would retain the favorable score components; a benchmark-specific pharmacophore would be speculation.

The high cages retain carbonyl/nitrogen functionality while greatly changing fluorine placement, sulfur bonding and ring connectivity. A sulfur-rich low example still scores only 1.0546805269255595e-09, so sulfur enrichment and ring density alone do not explain the gradient. The leading cage variants at 0.5147980244167879 and 0.5063755913792639 share molecular formula C17H15F2N3O3S5 but differ in bonding and hydrogen placement: the observed distinction goes beyond elemental composition. A related unsaturated variant has formula C17H13F2N3O3S5 and scores 0.48070999601549774. In the final seed-2 series, altering an imino-sulfur connection to a saturated sulfur connection gives 0.012990895249002812, whereas the final related structure reaches 0.3052653481197919. transferable_gaps.evidence: A sulfur-centered connection and its carbon analogue both score 0.9341451805829589, and a sulfur-free aryl-amine structure reaches 0.9492384404345239. An ordinary indole carboxamide reaches 0.39905049777278273 near an N-chloro carboxamide at 0.41003927643747895. Conversely, a peroxide-containing relative remains at 0.20647766243219587 near its nonperoxide relative at 0.20775769309691736. The observed scores do not consistently exclude reactive chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator reaches useful aromatic and polar arrangements without consistently supplying conventional matched alternatives to unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden graph-local access to matched conventional connections while retaining the surrounding attachment arrangement. Compare actual feedback for those alternatives; the generator should not require unusual sulfur, peroxide or heteroatom-halogen bonds to reach nearby configurations of its useful fragments. This is an accessibility gap, not evidence for a universal sulfur ban or an unobserved score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An aromatic amide series reaches 0.39905049777278273 while a related carbonyl-deleted connection scores 0.03343008011310944. Ring-opened carbonyl-chain examples score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515 below constrained aromatic/carbonyl examples. A methylene-linked amine/sulfur-ring structure scores 0.9441493227693659, whereas its direct-link analogue scores 0.907358519207774. All proposal sets already have ring_closure_rate 1.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain useful aromaticity, carbonyl placement and amine spacing when it changes ring or linker topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent matched ring and linker alternatives that preserve other observed useful connections while testing one geometric or attachment change. Access to feasible topology matters more than simply adding rings; local score comparisons should determine which arrangements to retain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several variants differing in alkyl extension, chain branching and terminal unsaturation share 0.6155070237050044. Other side-chain and ether/thioether variants share 0.6161710037174721. The most decorated maximum has 54 heavy atoms, long oxygen/sulfur chains and densely substituted aromatic groups. These ties do not show that the additional flexible appendages are necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator incompletely explores simpler members of score-indistinguishable decoration families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched shortening and simplification moves around an already scored framework, with preserved core attachments and feedback-based comparison. The missing capability is reliable access to simpler nearby structures; the evidence does not establish that smaller molecules will always score better.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The supplied high molecules include substituted saturated nitrogen rings, amino/halogen-bearing carbons, bridged lactams and densely fused sulfur cages. Some high variants have the same elemental formula but different bond placement and recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity and geometric feasibility unresolved for constrained and substituted products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible configurations when structural changes create or alter stereogenic relationships, and retain access to less strained topology alternatives. Do not equate a valid SMILES or a perceived ring with a realizable three-dimensional molecule. No benefit from a particular configuration is established by the current unassigned examples.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
